requirement_summary: Tested code MUST NOT use a Solidity compiler version older than 0.8.0, unless it meets all the requirements of a named Set of Overriding Requirements imported from EthTrust Security Levels Specification VERSION 2 (a different spec version, not present in our current V3 snapshot -- see note below).
source_inspection_notes: Read .venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/slither/detectors/attributes/incorrect_solc.py in full (IncorrectSolc class). Two independent checks live in the same detector: (1) lines 134-150: flags if `compilation_unit.solc_version` (the ACTUAL compiled version) is less than ALLOWED_VERSIONS[-1] == '0.8.0' -- a direct, hardcoded literal match to this requirement's '0.8.0' threshold. (2) lines 68-119: a separate pragma-text-based check (_check_pragma/_check_version) that flags pragma statements naming a version present in slither.utils.buggy_versions.bugs_by_version -- unrelated to this specific requirement's threshold, but relevant to req-1-compiler-sol-2021-4 (see that requirement's own L4 record).
analyzer_version: slither-analyzer==0.11.5 (pip-resolvable, confirmed via importlib.metadata in this repo's .venv; crytic-compile==0.3.11, solc-select==1.2.0)
compiler_ast_version: Not applicable to this specific check -- IncorrectSolc reads `compilation_unit.solc_version`, a crytic-compile-reported metadata value about which solc binary was actually invoked, not an AST-version-dependent traversal. No specific solc/AST version is required for this check itself to run correctly (it works across the solc versions Slither/crytic-compile support).

known_limitations_checked.interprocedural_scope: not_relevant -- this check inspects compiler metadata, not code control/data flow

semantic_boundary_tests: Not yet executed against a live compiled fixture in this pass -- the code-reading analysis above establishes the check's logic deterministically (it is a simple version-string comparison, not a heuristic pattern match), so a boundary test would confirm rather than discover behavior. Recorded as a TODO for the Track A verification phase: compile a trivial contract at 0.7.6 (expect flag) and at 0.8.0 exactly (expect no flag from this specific check) to confirm the off-by-one boundary empirically before this record is promoted past DRAFT_TRANSLATION maturity.

derivation_trace.ethtrust_phrase: Tested code MUST NOT use a Solidity compiler version older than 0.8.0, unless it meets [the named Set of Overriding Requirements from EthTrust-SL v2]
derivation_trace.analyzer_behavior: IncorrectSolc._detect() (lines 134-150) unconditionally flags whenever compilation_unit.solc_version < '0.8.0', with no awareness of, or check for, any override condition.
covered_cases: Tested Code actually compiled with any solc version below 0.8.0, where no override applies -- Slither's alert and EthTrust's violation coincide exactly.
uncovered_cases: Tested Code compiled below 0.8.0 where the override SET (imported from a different, not-yet-acquired spec version, EthTrust-SL v2) IS satisfied -- Slither still alerts, but per EthTrust this is NOT a violation. Slither cannot evaluate the override at all, so it necessarily over-reports relative to the requirement's true (conditional) obligation.

The override's actual content is unknown to this framework -- req-1-compiler-060's L1 record correctly captured that an override exists (via the 'Set of Overriding Requirements' plural pattern) but its target requirements live in EthTrust-SL Version 2, a document not in our current V3 snapshot. This is logged as a research gap below, not guessed at.
derivation_trace.final_classification: PARTIAL_MATCH -- outcome equivalence fails specifically because of the unresolvable override; trigger and scope equivalence both hold cleanly for the 'no override applies' case. Usable as an evidence-collector component (flags candidate violations) that must be paired with a separate, currently UNAVAILABLE applicability check for the v2-imported override set before a conformance verdict can be issued.

research_gap_note: This requirement's Set of Overriding Requirements is imported by reference from a DIFFERENT spec version (EthTrust Security Levels Specification Version 2), which is not present in our Phase 0 snapshot (we snapshotted the current, published Version 3). Resolving the override's actual conditions would require a separate Phase-0-style acquisition of the V2 spec text -- explicitly out of scope for this Track A tranche.
update_2026_08_06: L1 parser bug AR-005 was truncating this requirement's normative_text at the introducing colon, hiding the override list's actual CONTENTS (only the fact that a Set existed was visible, not what's in it). Fixed and re-run -- the named list is now visible: [S] No Overflow/Underflow, and 8 named compiler bugs (SOL-2020-11-push, SOL-2020-10, SOL-2020-9, SOL-2020-8, SOL-2020-6, SOL-2020-7, SOL-2020-5, SOL-2020-4), all from EthTrust-SL v2 specifically (none of these exact names exist as independent requirements in our current V3 corpus). This narrows the research gap without closing it: the override's TARGET LIST is now known, but each named V2 requirement's actual normative TEXT still isn't available without acquiring the V2 spec, so this doesn't change the PARTIAL_MATCH classification -- it does mean a future V2 acquisition effort would have a precise checklist to work from rather than an unbounded unknown.
